subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: Should explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec warn and continue without PTY, or fail closed because the requested terminal semantics cannot be honored?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the resolution changes user-visible tool semantics at a sandbox boundary and should reflect maintainer intent rather than automation preference.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Preserve current sandbox execution while adding a visible warning and docs/tests that `pty:true` is ignored in sandbox mode.

options.title: Fail Closed
options.body: Reject explicit sandboxed PTY requests so callers cannot mistake pipe execution for a terminal session.

options.title: Document Only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and clarify the limitation in docs, accepting continued silent tool-result ambiguity.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Preserve current sandbox execution while adding a visible warning and docs/tests that `pty:true` is ignored in sandbox mode.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle introduced exec PTY support and has the strongest history across the affected source, tests, and docs.
